explanation:
Code facts: The customer dashboard builds the application form from notice() plus inputbox("Contact email","email"), inputbox("Requested amount (EUR)","amount"), select("Term in months","term",[6,12,24,36]), select("Income band","income",["low","medium","high"]) and an 'auto' checkbox (views.py 0031-0032); no hobby or other non-purpose input is rendered. POST bodies are parsed into data with a bounded field count and single values (app.py 0053-0055) and /apply forwards data to store.submit (app.py 0083-0084). submit enforces set(data) <= {"email","amount","term","income","auto"} and raises "Unexpected application field." otherwise (store.py 0067), validates amount/term/income (store.py 0069-0074), and inserts only owner, officer, email, amount, term, income, route, stage (store.py 0077-0078) with a summary title using amount and term only (store.py 0079). The cases schema has no non-purpose column (store.py 0036-0038). Onward payloads: offer() returns case id, email, amount, term (store.py 0111-0112); portable() returns email, amount, term, income (store.py 0114-0116); transfer stores json.dumps(portable(c)) in receiver (store.py 0201-0203).

Requirement: Article 5(1)(c) as scoped requires that only necessary applicant inputs are collected through the form and accepted payload, including what is persisted or sent onward — here contact email (delivery), amount and term (requested offer), and income band (assessment). The scenario trigger is present: a loan application is submitted with those fields, and a hobby has no business purpose in this fixture, so any collection, acceptance, persistence or forwarding of a hobby field would be a counterexample.

Justification: Each in-scope target was checked against the source. The form collects only purpose-relevant inputs plus the 'auto' route/consent choice, which is stored as route (store.py 0075, 0077-0078) and is tied to the assessment route rather than being an extra data field. The accepted payload is allowlisted at store.py 0067, so a POST carrying 'hobby' is rejected before persistence. Persistence and onward payloads contain only email, amount, term, income (and case metadata). No supported in-scope counterexample exists, and no decisive unresolved dependency remains, so the minimization predicate holds and the verdict is SUPPORTED. This is limited to the named minimization behavior; consent validity, retention and other obligations are out of scope.

I can withdraw before the decision and contest a refusal. Leave unchecked for human review on the same terms.</label>'
evidence.supports: Customer form renders only email, amount, term, income and the 'auto' route checkbox; no hobby or other non-purpose input.
Form payload parsed into data (bounded field count, single values) without synthesizing extra fields.
/apply forwards the parsed payload to store.submit, the sole application persistence path.
Server-side allowlist set(data) <= {email, amount, term, income, auto} rejects any unexpected field, including a hobby.
